issues.problem: The github-script injection check, which this round claims to add, misses the ordinary single-line flow mapping of with:. FLOW_LINE fails closed only on a line that starts with a flow collection or on a key whose value starts with &, * or !. RUN_KEY matches only a run:/script: key at the start of a line. So 'with: {script: "core.info('${{ github.event.issue.title }}')"}' gets no report. PyYAML resolves it to with.script containing the expression, and GitHub expands it before JS runs. This is the 'step uses: with with: script:' variant the review was asked to test. The same line split over two lines is CAUGHT, which shows the gap is only the one-line form.
issues.evidence: REVF-H3b-r3-probe/wf3.py against a c69921d copy: with_flow_script valid MISSED []; with_flow_script_ml CAUGHT. yaml.safe_load gives {'with': {'script': "core.info('${{ github.event.issue.title }}')"}}. Output: REVF-H3b-r3-probe/wf3.out
issues.suggested_fix: Flag any line outside script and scalar text where '${{' appears after a run or script key at any position, for example r'(?:^|[{,\s])["\']?(?:run|script)["\']?\s*:' anywhere on the line. Or fail closed on flow mappings and sequences as the value of with: or a step key, allowing only on:/branches/paths-style lists. Add a test for the one-line with: {script: ...} form.

issues.problem: The fail-closed rule for anchors, aliases and tags still misses three valid forms. (a) A node property on a line of its own: 'T:' then '&t "echo ${{ github.event.issue.title }}"', and later 'run:' then '*t'. PyYAML resolves run to the expression string. (b) A merge key, '- <<: *base', where the anchor sits on its own line. The '<<' key is outside FLOW_LINE's key character set. (c) A double-quoted escape in a run value: 'run: "echo \u0024{{ github.event.issue.title }}"' decodes to '${{ ... }}' (\x24 too). All three pass the check. They take deliberate obfuscation rather than an accident, so this is minor.

issues.suggested_fix: Outside script and scalar text, reject lines whose stripped text starts with &, * or !, and any '<<' key. In run and script values and extents, also reject \u0024, \U00000024 and \x24 followed by '{{'.

issues.problem: The lowercase flattened rule (users_/users-/_home_) fires only when a known directory follows the name, so an unknown or dot directory evades it. 'x_users_<n>_silver_bullet_hooks' (a repository directly under home), 'x_users_<n>__claude_plugins_cache' (a ~/.claude path as graphify would flatten it), 'x_home_<n>_silver_bullet', 'x_home_<n>__config_x' and 'users-<n>-silver-bullet' all pass, tested with both real name tokens. Also missed: '\\wsl$\Ubuntu\home\<n>', '~<n>/projects', 'Users.<n>.projects', '/Users/<n>', '/Users\<n>\x' (mixed separators), and 'C:' followed by more than 24 backslashes (the 24-character window before 'users'). No such form is tracked today.

issues.suggested_fix: A lexical rule cannot get both recall and precision here. Add a hashed denylist: commit SHA-256 hashes of the maintainer's lower-cased username tokens, then split each file into [a-z0-9]+ tokens and compare their hashes. That catches every flattened form, discloses no value and creates no false positives. Keep the slash-path regexes for unknown users, and accept [\\/] after Users|home in HOME_PATH.

Scope '*.err' to .planning/** and research/**. Drop docs/**/*-stdout.txt unless docs runs write captures. Extend the tracked-captures assertion to *.out and *.attempt*.
